clue.text: One lingers somehow to get a drink

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters arrive by some unstated route, so they are rearranged

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who hangs about at the bar manages to get served.
explanation.definitionFit: Riesling is a white wine made from the grape of that name, so it is a drink.

clue.text: Bent leader goes off to a hiding place

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, and it going off means it is dropped

parts.note: a bent for something is a natural talent or flair

explanation.surface: A corrupt boss slips away to a hideout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bent' reads as crooked, but it is a noun meaning aptitude; 'leader goes off' removes its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A lair is the den where a wild animal hides and rests, hence any hideout.

clue.text: Firm has time problem with iron over a year

parts.note: rust is the corrosion that afflicts iron
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: A company is running late and has trouble with its steelwork over twelve months.
explanation.definitionFit: Trusty describes something reliable and steadfast, which is one sense of firm.

clue.text: Adagio I'll play without a number of bloomers

indicators.note: to play a piece is to perform it freely, signalling these letters are rearranged
without tells us the letters of the word a are left out of the rearranged pool

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A musician promises to perform a slow movement without the sheet music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' rearranges ADAGIOILL; 'without' removes A from that pool, leaving the eight letters. 'bloomers' are flowers, not knickers.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladioli is the plural of gladiolus, a flowering plant, so several of them are a number of blooming plants.

clue.text: Pass under attack by group leader

indicators.note: in a down answer the piece written under another comes after it

parts.note: a charge is a headlong attack
to pass something is to hand it over

explanation.surface: A footballer's pass is made while the team is on the attack.
explanation.walkthrough: A CHARGEHAND is a British term for a worker in charge of a small team, below a foreman.
explanation.definitionFit: A chargehand supervises a small group of workers, so is a group leader.

clue.text: The food merchant has extra supply of fat, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word in question is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: something grosser is fatter, carrying more fat

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper is said to have plenty of lard in stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has extra supply of fat' describes something fatter, which is grosser.
explanation.definitionFit: A grocer is a shopkeeper selling food and household provisions.

clue.text: Having more than one hearing aid?

definitions.text: Having more than one hearing aid?

parts.words: Having more than one hearing aid?
parts.note: the 'hearing aids' are not devices but the ears themselves; using two of them for listening is the sense

explanation.definitionFit: Binaural means involving both ears, so having two organs of hearing.

clue.text: Room? There's none in the fencing action

indicators.note: in places the zero inside the fencing move

parts.note: a lunge is the thrusting attack in fencing
none is nothing, a zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Asked if there's space, a fencer says there's no room for that move.
explanation.definitionFit: A lounge is a sitting room in a house or hotel.

clue.text: A house right in the heart of the French city

indicators.note: placing pieces in the heart of a word puts them in its middle

parts.note: le is the French masculine word for the

explanation.surface: An estate agent promises a home with all mod cons right in central Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the French' is a convention for LE (or LA, LES).
explanation.definitionFit: Lahore is a major city in Pakistan, capital of Punjab province.

clue.text: What's a ruler? Look inside!

indicators.note: the instruction to look inside tells us the letters sit within the run of words

explanation.surface: A child asks what a ruler is and is told to read the book.
explanation.walkthrough: The run 'wha(TS A R)uler' holds the answer; the whole clue both defines and hides it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsar was the emperor of Russia, so a ruler.

clue.text: Reliable path for a film extra

parts.note: sound means dependable, as in a sound investment
a track is a path

explanation.surface: A background actor needs a dependable route onto the set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film extra' is not a walk-on actor but something added to the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A soundtrack is the recorded music and sound added alongside a film's images.

clue.text: Prayers went out in a 20-nil thrashing!

indicators.note: a thrashing knocks things about, so these letters are thrown into a new order
out tells us the letters of went are put out of the pool before rearranging

parts.note: taken as written
written out in words, this score is twenty nil

explanation.surface: The faithful are left praying after their team loses heavily.
explanation.walkthrough: Spell '20-nil' as TWENTYNIL, add A; 'went out' removes W, E, N, T, and 'thrashing' rearranges the remaining A, T, Y, N, I, L.
explanation.definitionFit: A litany is a series of petitions recited in church, a form of prayer.

clue.text: Relieved everyone except the first turned aside

parts.note: all means everyone

indicators.note: except the first means without its opening letter

parts.note: to deviate is to turn aside from a course

explanation.surface: Everybody was reassured, apart from the leader who went off course.
explanation.definitionFit: To alleviate is to ease or lessen pain, so alleviated means relieved.

clue.text: There are a number of lines in this

definitions.text: There are a number of lines in this

parts.words: There are a number of lines in this
parts.note: not a poem or a play but a branch of mathematics that studies lines, angles and shapes

explanation.definitionFit: Geometry is the mathematics of points, lines, angles and figures, so it deals with many lines.

clue.text: New angle on acting initially? Take the lead from this

indicators.note: a new version of a word reworks its letters into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: initially signals the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A drama critic proposes a fresh approach so a director can take the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' is the metal, not the starring role.
explanation.definitionFit: Galena is lead sulphide, the main ore from which the metal is extracted.

clue.text: Cross-country race?

parts.note: read both as a steeplechase run over fences and as a people belonging to one whole country

explanation.walkthrough: The Grand National is Britain's famous steeplechase, run at Aintree.
explanation.definitionFit: National means belonging to a whole nation, and the Grand National is a famous cross-country horse race.

clue.text: End by putting back article in folder

indicators.note: in places the turned article inside the folder

parts.note: a file is a folder for papers

indicators.note: putting a word back reverses its letters

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An office worker finishes by returning a piece to its file.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting back' reverses the article before it goes inside; the surface reads as tidying papers, not as wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A finale is the closing part of a show or piece of music, its end.

clue.text: Have elms been diseased as a whole?

indicators.note: diseased trees are blighted and distorted, so the letters are distorted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Have the elm trees all been struck by blight together?
explanation.walkthrough: A nod to Dutch elm disease, which wiped out most of Britain's elms.
explanation.definitionFit: Ensemble comes from French for together, and as an adverb or noun means taken all together, as a whole.

clue.text: A little cloudiness, although it could be blue in North America

indicators.note: in places the rearranged colour inside the abbreviation
it could be suggests another possible arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: An American notices a slight haze that might look blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it could be' rearranges the colour before it sits inside the abbreviation; 'although' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A nebula is a cloud of gas and dust in space, a small patch of cloudiness in the sky.

clue.text: Ship in which company's ever prepared to hold a race

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company

indicators.note: to hold something is to contain it, so the race sits inside
prepared means worked into shape, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: the TT, or Tourist Trophy, is the motorcycle race on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A firm aboard a vessel is always ready to host a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges the four letters as RVEE, and 'to hold' puts the race inside them before the final E.
explanation.definitionFit: A corvette is a small, fast warship used for escort duties.

clue.text: A question in work (English) is obscure

indicators.note: in places the pair inside the work-plus-English pieces

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: A query in an English essay goes unanswered because it is unclear.
explanation.definitionFit: Opaque means not transparent, hence hard to understand or obscure.

clue.text: Fashionable second aerial?

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second
a dish is a satellite aerial

explanation.surface: A second satellite antenna is the latest trend.
explanation.definitionFit: Modish means in the current fashion, stylish.

clue.text: Pack up drink for the side

indicators.note: in a down answer up means the word is written upwards, in reverse

parts.note: to ram something is to pack it tightly
gin is a spirit drink

explanation.surface: Put away the bottle of spirits to make room.
explanation.definitionFit: A margin is the edge or side of a page or area.

clue.text: He should make the list

parts.note: not someone hoping to be included but someone whose job is to compile one

explanation.definitionFit: A cataloguer compiles catalogues, systematic lists of items.

clue.text: Theatrical temporary dwellings

definitions.meaning: exaggerated and affected in a showy way
a set of tents or huts put up for a short stay

explanation.surface: A touring theatre troupe sleeps in tents.
explanation.definitionFit: Camp means both exaggeratedly theatrical behaviour and a site of tents or huts.

clue.text: Seek to manipulate the cable

definitions.meaning: to persuade gently, working on someone
short for coaxial cable, as used for TV aerials

explanation.surface: An engineer tries to wangle the wire into place.
explanation.definitionFit: Coax means to persuade by gentle urging and is also short for coaxial cable.

clue.text: Shout when you solve a clue?

definitions.text: Shout when you solve a clue?

parts.words: Shout when you solve a clue?
parts.note: the cry of discovery attributed to Archimedes, fitting any moment of sudden insight

explanation.definitionFit: Eureka is the exclamation of triumph on finding something out, as Archimedes reputedly cried.

clue.text: Wire to a friend abroad showing friendliness

parts.note: ami is French for a friend
a cable is a telegram, a wire

explanation.surface: A telegram to a pal overseas is a warm gesture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wire' is an old word for a telegram, as is CABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Amicable means friendly and goodwilled in manner.
